newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks tumble after Dow sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks tumble after Dow sell-off.

text.p: The Australian share market tumbled at the opening on Monday after the Dow dived over three percent in its second biggest point loss ever on Friday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index opened 73 points, or 2.74 percent, lower at 2,593.2.
September share price index futures were down 72 points at 2,590, a 3.2-point discount to the underlying index.
Opening losses after the Wall Street walloping were predictable, but brokers said the real test could come on Tuesday if the Dow Jones industrial average fell again in Monday trading.
"The real test will be tomorrow," said Reynolds and Co dealer Peter Struk.
"If New York is down a poultice again tonight then we will really cop a caning. If it is up, we should bounce a bit tomorrow but (what happens in New York) is the crux of it."
Traders were wondering whether a turning point had been reached after the market's volatility last week.
"We thought at least 50 to 60 points down early but the U.S. has been volatile all week," said a dealer at a European investment bank.
"If it has another shaky night then you might really see things pushed along."
Among the majors, Commonwealth Bank suffered most, its fall exacerbated by going ex-dividend. CommBank shares were 79.4 cents (US$0.59) lower at A$15.80 by 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT).
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of over 20 to one, while only 11 percent of stocks remained steady.
In other local markets, Australian bond yields rose slightly early trading with one wary eye on global stocks after the hefty plunge in the U.S. equity market on Friday.

The Australian dollar was showing that despite upside rebuffs last week it still had good support, and was expected to hold above US$0.74 on a day when the U.S. dollar and stockmarket fall would dominate regional trading.
